cityQuote: Give him alms, woman, for there is nothing in life like the sorrow of being blind in Granada.
cityQuoteAttribution: Francisco de Icaza, Mexican poet, in lines now set into a wall of the Alhambra
heroTitle: Granada hero — Er Komandante (CC BY 2.5, Wikimedia Commons)
wordsPreamble:
- Granada speaks Andalusian Spanish. The final s is often dropped, so “más o menos” can sound like “mah o meno.”
- Unlike in Seville, most people in the city say the Spanish z and soft c as “th,” as in Madrid.
- Order a drink at almost any bar and a small plate of food comes with it, free. Each round brings a different tapa.
- Granadinos are known for a dry, blunt manner they call “malafollá.” It isn’t meant personally.
